## Statement
C has no big integers. Write a calculator for **signed integers of up to 5 000 digits**. Each input line has the form `A OP B`, where OP is `+`, `-` or `*` and A and B are decimal integers with an optional leading `-` (no `+` sign, possibly with leading zeros). Print the exact result for each line, with no leading zeros (and `0`, never `-0`).

Design it as a small module: a `BigInt` struct (sign plus a dynamically allocated digit array, least significant digit first) with functions to parse, add, subtract, multiply, print and free. Every allocation must be freed. Up to 200 lines; schoolbook O(n·m) multiplication is fast enough.

## Starter
```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

typedef struct {
    int sign;          /* +1 or -1 */
    size_t len;        /* number of digits used */
    unsigned char *d;  /* d[0] = least significant digit */
} BigInt;

int main(void) {
    char a[6000], op[4], b[6000];
    while (scanf("%5999s %3s %5999s", a, op, b) == 3) {
        /* TODO */
    }
    return 0;
}
```

## Hints
- Parse: remember the sign, skip leading zeros, and store digits reversed. Treat the number zero as `len = 1, d[0] = 0, sign = +1`.
- Write **magnitude** helpers that ignore signs: `cmp_abs`, `add_abs`, `sub_abs` (requires |a| ≥ |b|). Then signed `+` and `-` are sign case analysis: `a - b` is `a + (-b)`. For `a + b` with different signs, subtract the smaller magnitude from the larger and take the sign of the larger.
- Multiplication: accumulate into an `int` array of size `la + lb`, `r[i + j] += a[i] * b[j]`, then propagate carries in one pass (columns stay below 2³¹ for 5000-digit inputs).
- Normalise after every operation: strip high zeros, and set sign = +1 for zero.

## Solution
```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

typedef struct {
    int sign;
    size_t len;
    unsigned char *d;
} BigInt;

static BigInt big_alloc(size_t len) {
    BigInt r = {1, len, calloc(len ? len : 1, 1)};
    if (!r.d) { perror("calloc"); exit(1); }
    return r;
}

static void big_normalize(BigInt *x) {
    while (x->len > 1 && x->d[x->len - 1] == 0) x->len--;
    if (x->len == 1 && x->d[0] == 0) x->sign = 1;     /* no negative zero */
}

static BigInt big_parse(const char *s) {
    int sign = 1;
    if (*s == '-') { sign = -1; s++; }
    while (*s == '0' && s[1]) s++;                    /* skip leading zeros, keep one */
    size_t n = strlen(s);
    BigInt r = big_alloc(n);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; i++) r.d[i] = (unsigned char)(s[n - 1 - i] - '0');
    r.sign = sign;
    big_normalize(&r);
    return r;
}

static int cmp_abs(const BigInt *a, const BigInt *b) {
    if (a->len != b->len) return a->len < b->len ? -1 : 1;
    for (size_t i = a->len; i-- > 0;)
        if (a->d[i] != b->d[i]) return a->d[i] < b->d[i] ? -1 : 1;
    return 0;
}

static BigInt add_abs(const BigInt *a, const BigInt *b) {
    size_t n = (a->len > b->len ? a->len : b->len) + 1;
    BigInt r = big_alloc(n);
    int carry = 0;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        int s = carry + (i < a->len ? a->d[i] : 0) + (i < b->len ? b->d[i] : 0);
        r.d[i] = (unsigned char)(s % 10);
        carry = s / 10;
    }
    big_normalize(&r);
    return r;
}

static BigInt sub_abs(const BigInt *a, const BigInt *b) {   /* requires |a| >= |b| */
    BigInt r = big_alloc(a->len);
    int borrow = 0;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < a->len; i++) {
        int s = a->d[i] - borrow - (i < b->len ? b->d[i] : 0);
        borrow = s < 0;
        r.d[i] = (unsigned char)(s + (borrow ? 10 : 0));
    }
    big_normalize(&r);
    return r;
}

static BigInt big_add(const BigInt *a, const BigInt *b) {
    BigInt r;
    if (a->sign == b->sign) {
        r = add_abs(a, b);
        r.sign = a->sign;
    } else if (cmp_abs(a, b) >= 0) {
        r = sub_abs(a, b);
        r.sign = a->sign;
    } else {
        r = sub_abs(b, a);
        r.sign = b->sign;
    }
    big_normalize(&r);
    return r;
}

static BigInt big_sub(const BigInt *a, const BigInt *b) {
    BigInt nb = *b;                 /* shallow copy: shares digits, only the sign differs */
    nb.sign = -b->sign;
    return big_add(a, &nb);
}

static BigInt big_mul(const BigInt *a, const BigInt *b) {
    size_t n = a->len + b->len;
    int *acc = calloc(n, sizeof *acc);
    if (!acc) { perror("calloc"); exit(1); }
    for (size_t i = 0; i < a->len; i++)
        for (size_t j = 0; j < b->len; j++)
            acc[i + j] += a->d[i] * b->d[j];
    BigInt r = big_alloc(n);
    long long carry = 0;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        long long s = acc[i] + carry;
        r.d[i] = (unsigned char)(s % 10);
        carry = s / 10;
    }
    free(acc);
    r.sign = a->sign * b->sign;
    big_normalize(&r);
    return r;
}

static void big_print(const BigInt *x) {
    if (x->sign < 0) putchar('-');
    for (size_t i = x->len; i-- > 0;) putchar('0' + x->d[i]);
    putchar('\n');
}

static void big_free(BigInt *x) { free(x->d); x->d = NULL; }

int main(void) {
    static char a[6000], op[4], b[6000];
    while (scanf("%5999s %3s %5999s", a, op, b) == 3) {
        BigInt x = big_parse(a), y = big_parse(b), r;
        if (op[0] == '+') r = big_add(&x, &y);
        else if (op[0] == '-') r = big_sub(&x, &y);
        else r = big_mul(&x, &y);
        big_print(&r);
        big_free(&x);
        big_free(&y);
        big_free(&r);
    }
    return 0;
}
```

**What this milestone tests:**
- **Representation:** digits least significant first make carries flow upward with increasing indices. A sign plus a magnitude makes `+`/`-` a clean case analysis over two magnitude primitives.
- **Normalisation as an invariant** (no leading zeros, zero is non-negative) keeps comparison and printing trivial, and kills the `-0` bug.
- **Memory discipline:** every `BigInt` owns its digit array, and `big_free` releases it. `big_sub` reuses `b`'s digits through a shallow copy with a flipped sign, safe because it's never freed separately.
- **Deferred carries in multiplication:** accumulating column sums first and carrying once is simpler and faster than carrying inside the inner loop. The column bound is 5000 · 81 < 2³¹.
